title: Two Scottish pubs have been named among the UK's most haunted
excerpt: Are you brave enough to visit Scotland's most haunted pubs this Halloween?
content:
Scotland's 'most haunted' pubs named as the ghosts said to torment them explained

Are you brave enough to visit Scotland's most haunted pubs this Halloween?

12:20, 20 Oct 2026

With Halloween approaching, Scots looking for a spooky night out might not have to look far to find somewhere with a chilling past. From unexplained noisses to spirits said to roam the same room centuries after their deaths, some of the country's oldest pubs have build up eerie reputations over the years.

‌

‌

And while many people will be dressing up and heading out for Halloween celebrations, others might fancy a pint somewhere with a few ghost stories of its own.

‌

Now, Eat Drink Meet, a website that helps people discover nearby pubs, bars and restaurants, has revealed 13 of the UK's most haunted pubs.

‌

Two Scottish venues have made the list, including a historic Edinburgh bar where a former bishop is said to have a particular dislike for modern music. Read on to discover Scotland's spookiest pubs and the reason why they take the crown.

‌

The Mitre Bar, Edinburgh

Sitting on Edinburgh's famous Royal Mile, The Mitre Bar is surrounded by centuries of history in a city known for its dark past. Edinburgh has been associated with tales of bloody battles, plague and unexplained events, making it a fitting setting for a pub with its own ghostly legend.

‌

The traditional bar serves ales and pub food, but local folklore suggests there could be more than customers and staff sharing the space. According to legend, the pub is haunted by John Spottiswood.

As the former Bishop of St Andrews, his throne is said to be buried beneath the bar area and his spirit is believed to roam the premises.

‌

However, it is not his alleged prescene that makes the pub's ghost story stand out. The bishop is said to have a strong dislike for modern music, and has reportedly been known to turn off the jukebox when a song plays that he does not approve of.

Anyone planning a visit might want to think carefully about their music choices, particularly if they do not fancy upsetting a centuries old spirit.

‌

The Hawes Inn, Queensferry

Another Scottish pub with a spooky reputation can be found in South Queensferry, west of Edinburgh. The Hawes Inn is known for its views across the Firth of Forth and its links to Scottish literary history.

‌

The pub is said to have inspired Robert Louis Stevenson's novel Kidnapped, with the author reportedly staying there and writing part of the book in one of its rooms.

But beyond its literary connections, the historic inn has also attracted stories of paranormal activity. According to local tales, several spirits are said haunt one of the rooms in its bed and breakfast accommodation.

‌

Guests have reportedly heard heavy breathing during the night, while the same room is said to be unusually difficult to warm up.

The unexplained chill has fuelled speculation that something otherworldly could be lingering in the room, although the building's location near a pier has also led to suggestions that the spirts could be connected to people who met tragic ends nearby.

‌

For those who are brave enough to spend the night, the inn offers nine double rooms. Whether guests enjoy a peaceful night's sleep or find themselves listening out for unexplained noises is another matter.

With Halloween just around the corner, both pubs offer a chance to enjoy a drink while soaking up some of Scotland's darker folklore. And for anyone who believes in ghosts, the stories might be enough to make them think twice before heading to the bars at all.

‌

The UK's most haunted pubs

The 13 pubs named on Eat Drink Meet's list are:

  1. The Mitre Bar, Edinburgh
  2. The Hawes Inn, Queensferry
  3. The Old White Swan, York
  4. The Punch Bowl, York
  5. The Spaniards Inn, Hampstead Heath
  6. The Volunteer, Baker Street
  7. Williamson's Tavern, London
  8. The Fighting Cocks, Moseley
  9. The Trocadero, Birmingham City Centre
  10. Fairfield Arms, Audenshaw
  11. Toby Carvery, Bolton
  12. The Captain's Wife, Penarth
  13. The Castle, Peak District
